chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Hassan, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Abu Jameela, from Al-Halbi and Zurara as well, and Muhammad ibn Muslim and Humran ibn Ayn, from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), that they said:
The habitual drinker of wine is like an idol worshipper.

key_terms.مُدْمِنُ: The habitual one / one who is accustomed to doing something continuously
key_terms.وَثَنٍ: Idol / a deity worshipped besides God

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual status of a habitual wine drinker in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, the Imams (peace be upon them) equate the habitual drinker of wine with an idol worshipper, a comparison rooted in the idea that constant intoxication leads to a loss of divine consciousness akin to the neglect of monotheism. This ruling highlights the spiritual gravity of *khamr* in Shia jurisprudence, where habitual consumption is not merely a sin but a state of being that mirrors the core defect of shirk. The comparison underscores how the regular consumer of wine becomes 'drunk' on worldly attachment, effectively replacing God with their habit.
